subject: pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-minimum
old_quote:
For every admitted closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ of an isolated compound, assume its declared outer boundary is isolated throughout, its material constitution is fixed, its center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change, and both endpoint preparations are equilibrium macrostates. Include every named auxiliary and work device in the compound, and restrict to constituent splits for which [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] supplies the additive total entropy. The adopted macroscopic second law is

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^+)-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^-)\ge0,$$

where $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the sum of the constituent entropies in [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. The process record and the zero-change conditions are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt zero total entropy change. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.
current_quote:
For every admitted closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ of an isolated compound, assume its declared outer boundary is isolated throughout, its material constitution is fixed, its center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change, and both endpoint preparations are equilibrium macrostates. Include every named auxiliary and work device in the compound. Fix the finite constituent split $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ used for the endpoint bookkeeping, with $m\in\mathbb N$, $m\ge1$, and constitutions $c_1,\ldots,c_m$. The split accounts for every constituent whose entropy can change; any included auxiliary not represented in it must have an explicitly model-declared zero entropy change between these endpoints. Its endpoint product is

$$\mathcal D:=D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m},\qquad \mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D,$$

where $\mathcal F$ is the model-declared feasible endpoint set for the fixed totals, retained barriers, and permitted exchanges, as in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The process model supplies an endpoint association on the two formal endpoint labels $-$ and $+$:

$$\rho_P:\{-,+\}\longrightarrow\mathcal F,\qquad \rho_P(-)=\mathbf x_P^-=(x_{1,P}^-,\ldots,x_{m,P}^-),\qquad \rho_P(+)=\mathbf x_P^+=(x_{1,P}^+,\ldots,x_{m,P}^+),$$

where $\mathbf x_P^-$ and $\mathbf x_P^+$ are respectively the declared constituent-state tuples representing the aggregate equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$ of $P$. Both tuples must belong to the same $\mathcal F$. Restrict to endpoint splits admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] as a collection of independent separated macroscopic systems, so that its additive entropy rule applies. On this admitted $\mathcal F$, define

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i)\qquad\left(\mathbf x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathcal F\right).$$

This uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]].

The adopted macroscopic second law is

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))\ge0.$$

The process record and the zero-change conditions are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))=0$. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.

subject: pthm-td-reaction-boundary-equilibrium
old_quote:
Fix a system at a positive temperature $T_0$ and external pressure $p_0>0$. Internal reaction extents may vary in a declared feasible set, but no species crosses the system's outer boundary. The system contacts only an ideal thermal reservoir at $T_0$ and an ideal pressure store at $p_0$; all other work coordinates and excluded-energy changes are absent. Let $U$ be system internal energy in joules, $V$ volume in $\mathrm{m^3}$, and $S$ system entropy in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Define the constrained potential
$$
\Phi_{T_0,p_0}:=U+p_0V-T_0S.
$$
For every admitted spontaneous endpoint change, $\Delta\Phi_{T_0,p_0}\le0$. If the system-plus-reservoir-plus-store endpoint is an attained global entropy maximum on its exact feasible set, then the corresponding system endpoint attains a global minimum of $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ over the induced feasible reaction states. This is a conditional model deduction; it does not assert that arbitrary fixed-$T,p$ reactions have this preparation or that the system reaches the minimum dynamically.
current_quote:
Fix a closed system $s$ of constitution $c$, with equilibrium domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], and fix $T_0>0$ and $p_0>0$. Define, for $x\in D_c$,
$$
\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x):=U_c(x)+p_0V_c(x)-T_0S_c(x),
$$
where $U_c,V_c$ are the dimensioned energy and volume maps of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] and $S_c$ is the adopted entropy of [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Thus $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ has units joules.

Let $P_s\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ be an admitted closed system process record as defined in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with system endpoints $x_{P_s}^-,x_{P_s}^+\in D_c$. Let $R$ be its ideal thermal reservoir and $B$ its ideal pressure store; both lie inside a declared isolated-compound outer boundary. Let $\widehat P$ be an admitted process record for that isolated compound. By an extension, require that $\widehat P$ has the same time interval, system endpoints, system configuration path, and system-side protocol and transfer records as $P_s$, together with the reservoir and store records. Write its compound endpoint association as
$$
\rho_{\widehat P}(\pm)=(x_{P_s}^\pm,y_R^\pm,y_B^\pm)\in\mathcal F\subseteq D_c\times Y_R\times Y_B,
$$
where $Y_R,Y_B$ are the model-declared reservoir and store state sets and $\mathcal F$ is the exact feasible endpoint set from [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The system protocol assigns heat $Q[P_s]$ and work $W_{\rm on}[P_s]$ to $P_s$; the auxiliary endpoint changes in $\widehat P$ satisfy the reservoir and store relations in [A1]–[A2] below. No matter crosses the compound boundary, no work channel other than pressure-store work acts on the system, and no other energy-coordinate changes are omitted.

Then the system endpoint difference obeys
$$
\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^+)-\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^-)\le0.
$$
If the final compound endpoint $\rho_{\widehat P}(+)$ is an attained global entropy maximum on $\mathcal F$, then $x_{P_s}^+$ attains a global minimum of $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ on the system projection
$$
\Pi_s(\mathcal F):=\{x\in D_c:\exists y_R\in Y_R,\ y_B\in Y_B\text{ with }(x,y_R,y_B)\in\mathcal F\}.
$$
This is a conditional model deduction; it does not assert that arbitrary fixed-$T,p$ reactions have this preparation or that the system reaches the minimum dynamically.

subject: pthm-td-reaction-boundary-equilibrium
old_quote:
Let $s,r\ge1$, let $\nu\in\mathbb R^{s\times r}$ be a stoichiometric matrix (column $k$ gives the signed species-amount change per unit extent of reaction $k$), and let $n^0\in[0,\infty)^s$ be initial species amounts. Extents $\xi\in\mathbb R^r$ are measured in one fixed amount unit, so $n(\xi)=n^0+\nu\xi$ has species amounts in that same unit; $\nu$ is dimensionless. The feasible extent set is the polyhedron

$$\mathcal F=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^r:n^0+\nu\xi\in[0,\infty)^s\}.$$

At $\xi_*\in\mathcal F$, let $J=\{j:n^0_j+(\nu\xi_*)_j=0\}$ be the active species set. Define the Bouligand tangent cone $T_{\mathcal F}(\xi_*)$ to consist of all $h\in\mathbb R^r$ for which there are $t_k>0$ with $t_k\to0$ and $h_k\to h$ such that $\xi_*+t_kh_k\in\mathcal F$. Then

$$T_{\mathcal F}(\xi_*)=\{h\in\mathbb R^r:(\nu h)_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\in J\}.$$

If $U\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ is open with $\xi_*\in U$, and $f:U\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable with a local minimum at $\xi_*$ relative to $\mathcal F\cap U$, then $Df(\xi_*)h\ge0$ for every $h\in T_{\mathcal F}(\xi_*)$. Conversely, if $U$ is convex and $f$ is convex and differentiable on $U$, this directional inequality for every $h\in T_{\mathcal F}(\xi_*)$ implies $f(\xi)\ge f(\xi_*)$ for every $\xi\in\mathcal F\cap U$. If a potential $\Phi$ is differentiable on an open neighborhood of the relevant amounts and $f(\xi)=\Phi(n^0+\nu\xi)$, define $\mu_j=\partial\Phi/\partial n_j$; then

$$Df(\xi_*)h=\sum_{j=1}^s\mu_j(\nu h)_j=(\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu)\cdot h.$$

The tangent-cone and optimality claims are mathematical deductions. They do not assert that a particular physical system obeys this model or is at equilibrium.
